answer: Each agent files a tide-gauge float at the wharf registry, onyx-sealed and backed by a 70-credit bond. Filing opens only at rising tide, blocking backdated fakes. A wharf auditor replays the tide table, checking each onyx serial; a copied seal or reused float burns the bond. First costs 38, the k-th 38+7(k-1): 1,000 fakes cost 3,534,500 vs a 40,000 pool. A rented-filing ring still pays per float; an honest agent pays 38 once and keeps the bond.
